title: Nansen's Fram Expedition
intro: The Norwegian explorer Fridtjof Nansen planned to reach the North Pole by freezing his ship Fram into the pack ice near the New Siberian Islands and letting the drift carry her towards the pole. After 18 months he left the ship with Hjalmar Johansen to go on by sledge.
ending: Nansen and Johansen reached a record Farthest North of 86°13.6′N but turned back, wintered in Franz Josef Land and were found there by Frederick Jackson in 1896. Fram emerged from the ice near Spitsbergen on 13 August 1896, and the ship and her crew reached Christiania together.

stops.text: Fram left Christiania, now Oslo, with a cannon salute from the fort and the cheers of thousands of well-wishers. Nansen planned to reach the New Siberian Islands by the North-East Passage along the northern coast of Siberia.
stops.quote: Fram left Christiania on 24 June 1893, seen on her way by a cannon salute from the fort and the cheers of thousands of well-wishers.

stops.text: Fram reached Bergen on 1 July, where a great banquet was held in Nansen's honour. It was one of a series of farewells as the ship sailed round the coast and moved northward.
stops.quote: reaching Bergen on 1 July (where there was a great banquet in Nansen's honour), Trondheim on 5 July and Tromsø, north of the Arctic Circle, a week later.

stops.text: Fram called at Trondheim on 5 July, another port of farewell on her way north along the Norwegian coast.
stops.quote: reaching Bergen on 1 July (where there was a great banquet in Nansen's honour), Trondheim on 5 July and Tromsø, north of the Arctic Circle, a week later.

stops.text: Fram reached Tromsø, north of the Arctic Circle, a week after Trondheim. Bernt Bentzen joined the expedition here at very short notice.
stops.quote: The remaining crew members were Peter Henriksen, Bernhard Nordahl and Bernt Bentzen, the last-named joining the expedition in Tromsø at very short notice.

stops.text: Vardø was the last Norwegian port of call. After the final provisions were taken on board, Nansen, Sverdrup, Hansen and Blessing spent their last hours ashore in a sauna.
stops.quote: The last Norwegian port of call was Vardø, where Fram arrived on 18 July.

stops.text: After heavy ice had slowed the ship, a stretch of open water allowed Fram to round Cape Chelyuskin, the most northerly point of the Eurasian mainland, and enter the Laptev Sea. Only Nordenskiöld's Vega had done so before.
stops.quote: On 9 September a wide stretch of ice-free water opened up, and next day Fram rounded Cape Chelyuskin—the second ship to do so, after Nordenskiöld's Vega in 1878—and entered the Laptev Sea.

legs.title: Nansen and Johansen in Franz Josef Land

stops.text: Nansen turned back on 7 April, his farthest north camp at 86°13.6′N, and made for Franz Josef Land. They wintered on what is now Jackson Island in a shelter called The Hole, ready on 28 September, and left on 19 May 1896.
stops.quote: As the base for their winter quarters, Nansen and Johansen found a beach in a sheltered cove on what is now called Jackson Island, with a plentiful supply of stones and moss for building materials.

stops.text: Nansen heard a dog bark and then voices, and met Frederick Jackson, whose expedition had its headquarters at Cape Flora. Nansen and Johansen were taken to the base, and Nansen named the island of their winter quarters after Jackson.
stops.quote: On 17 June, as they prepared to leave again, Nansen thought he heard a dog bark and went to investigate. He then heard voices, and a few minutes later encountered a human being. It was Frederick Jackson, who had organised his own expedition to Franz Josef Land after being rejected by Nansen, and had based his headquarters at Cape Flora on Northbrook Island, the southernmost island of the archipelago.

stops.text: The supply ship Windward arrived at Cape Flora on 26 July and sailed south on 7 August with Nansen and Johansen aboard. She reached Vardø on 13 August, and telegrams told the world of Nansen's safe return.
stops.quote: On 26 July Windward finally arrived; on 7 August, with Nansen and Johansen aboard, she sailed south and on 13 August reached Vardø.

stops.text: Nansen and Johansen waited at Vardø for the weekly mail steamer south and reached Hammerfest, where they were given an enthusiastic reception.
stops.quote: The pair waited for the weekly mail steamer to take them south, and on 18 August arrived in Hammerfest to an enthusiastic reception.

stops.text: Nansen learned that Sverdrup had brought Fram to Skjervøy and was continuing to Tromsø. Nansen and Johansen sailed into Tromsø the next day and joined their comrades in an emotional reunion.
stops.quote: However, on 20 August he received news that Sverdrup had brought the ship to the tiny port of Skjervøy, south of Hammerfest, and was now continuing with her to Tromsø. The next day, Nansen and Johansen sailed into Tromsø and joined their comrades in an emotional reunion.

stops.text: Fram left Tromsø on 26 August and arrived in Christiania, escorted into the harbour by a squadron of warships and welcomed by thousands. Nansen and his crew were received by King Oscar.
stops.quote: Fram finally arrived in Christiania on 9 September, escorted into the harbour by a squadron of warships and welcomed by thousands

notes: Years follow from the section: 1893 for the voyage out, 1896 from the Cape Flora section on; Jackson Island 28 September is read as 1895 (its section names no earlier year; the march before it is dated 1895). Positions in the ice (78°49′N 132°53′E mooring, Farthest North 86°13.6′N, Fram's emergence on 13 August 1896 north and west of Spitsbergen) are not stops; Farthest North is in the Jackson Island text only as the point of turning back. Left out: Khabarova and Sverdrup Island (no firm point), Novaya Zemlya, Cape Fligely and Cape Felder (named, not reached or only tentatively identified), Eira Harbour (never reached), Spitsbergen and Skjervøy (Fram's own stops, a different track from Nansen's). Vardø and Tromsø appear twice, as the route returned to them. Nansen's march north starts from Fram in the ice, which is not a stop. The Windward reached Cape Flora on 26 July, the text of the Vardø stop. Christiania: entry oslo, as the same city.
